info.title: UpNext API
info.description:
The HTTP API of UpNext, the game library that picks what to play next. This is the v1 contract: adding a field or an endpoint is fine within v1; removing or renaming one means v2. Paths are relative to `/api/v1`; `/api/...` answers the same until the first public release.

This computer (a loopback address, addressed as localhost) needs no token. Another device needs a token (`Authorization: Bearer upnext_…`, scope `read` or `full`) or a paired browser's cookie (`upnext_device`, full). Each operation's `security` says which; an operation marked `x-local-only` answers only on the computer UpNext runs on.

An operation with the `UpNext-Player` parameter answers for one player: a token bound to a player, else that header, else the browser's player cookie, else the default player.

Errors are `{"error": "…"}` with the status.

loves.description: Moods, then genres and themes, for "what you love".

seconds_per_call.description:
For the backend in use. None when it isn't known yet: a local model

At the API's list prices, from this install's calls; None for a

The latest rating a game had as a pick, with what its lineup was asked

ResetBody.description:
What `POST /setup/reset` clears before the wizard starts again.
The wizard itself never deletes anything; this is the one way to start
over, and a backup is taken first. With two or more players, the taste
profile and the history are the request's player's own; the
whole library is everyone's.

accounts.description:
Store sign-ins and keys: Steam's Web API key and SteamID (and the
Steam name and picture shown for it), IGDB's and RAWG's keys, the
Galaxy file, and the request's player's GOG and Epic sign-ins. With
two or more players, only the request player's own: their SteamID,
Galaxy file and sign-ins; the keys that are everyone's stay.

ai.description:
The AI choice: the backend, its models, keys, server address and
thinking setting.

taste.description:
The taste profile: what you told it, the patterns it found, and the
play diary.

history.description:
Statuses and history: the statuses and star ratings you set, why you
stopped, Play later, Second Chance answers, "This game can be played

how you rated them.

The whole library: every game, what was fetched and written about

Settings that still have a value from the environment or a `.env`

device.name: upnext_device
